newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas turns mixed, cash gains.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas turns mixed, cash gains.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures turned narrowly mixed late Monday, with trade still sluggish amid little conviction about market direction but firmer cash keeping the bears in check for now, sources said.
At 1410 EDT, July slipped 0.9 cent to $2.14 per million British thermal units, while August was 1.2 cents lower at $2.155. Other deferreds were narrowly mixed.

"Cash was up from the weekend, but there's still not a lot of end-user demand. It seems like some people want to be short in the high-teens (basis July)," said one East Coast trader, adding there was little or no conviction about direction.

With Midwest and Northeast temperatures this week expected to stay around normal, few expected a significant rally near-term despite some heat in Texas, but some noted revised forecasts for above-normal weather across southern tier states and in the East later this week and next.
Chart traders said they expected some follow-through buying this morning after July's upside reversal last week, but they noted good selling in the low-to-mid $2.20s.
After $2.21 and $2.25, technicians pegged July resistance at $2.37 and then at the $2.44 contract high. Support was seen at last week's low of $2.055 and then at $2.

In the cash Monday, Louisiana Gulf Coast gas firmed by about five cents to the mid-teens or higher. Midcon pipes gained a similar amount to the low-$2s. New York city gate gas also was about a nickel higher in the low-to-mid $2.40s.
NYMEX said 16,935 contracts traded at 1340 EDT.
On the KCBT, July eased 0.3 cent to $2.01, while deferreds were narrowly mixed. The East/West spread narrowed by 0.6 cent to 13.0 cents (NYMEX premium).
